claims.text: Index can be built on a function or expression of columns
claims.quote: An index column need not be just a column of the underlying table, but can be a function or scalar expression computed from one or more columns of the table.

claims.text: lower(col1) query can use an index defined on lower(col1)
claims.quote: SELECT * FROM test1 WHERE lower(col1) = 'value'; This query can use an index if one has been defined on the result of the lower(col1) function: CREATE INDEX test1_lower_col1_idx ON test1 (lower(col1));

claims.text: Fetching rows separately via index is more expensive than sequential reading
claims.quote: Fetching rows separately is much more expensive than reading them sequentially, but because not all the pages of the table have to be visited, this is still cheaper than a sequential scan.

claims.text: Without a WHERE clause the planner uses a sequential scan
claims.quote: Since this query has no WHERE clause, it must scan all the rows of the table, so the planner has chosen to use a simple sequential scan plan.

claims.text: EXPLAIN shows the chosen plan, e.g. a simple index scan
claims.quote: EXPLAIN SELECT * FROM tenk1 WHERE unique1 = 42;
